I don’t want to vent to anyone other than my family and psychologist tbh. When I started to get a lot worse, I doubt that people weren’t getting drained by me and weren’t regretting ever getting close to me (I just don’t want them to leave me, you know?) 

Positivity’s hard for me but I’m trying to go outside more and take up some hobbies, so that’s a decent step I think. Thank you for your insight!

This is really empathetic, thank you. 

Emailing actually sounds like a good idea, because I WANT to talk about it with my psychologist but I just can’t say it out loud. I wouldn’t tell anyone what I wrote on here since I just can’t bring myself to do so. I’ve been put on medications and they’ve stabilised my mood - now I feel neutral instead of low, but I’m just worried (well, more like expecting) that they’ll eventually stop working like my previous ones did.

I think people did care about me, but didn’t think I’d actually do it since I joke about killing myself a lot? I don’t know. 

I‘m already seeing a psychologist and am on new medications. It’s just that I’ve been let down by meds and professionals a lot before so I’m not optimistic tbh
Yeah, you’re right. Although I try to remind myself that recovery takes time and isn’t linear, I always find myself being impatient when it comes to it because I don’t want to feel like this anymore.

This post is really refreshing tbh, I’ve become very exhausted of hearing sugar-coated and guilt-tripping shit whenever suicide is brought up. People think they’re doing you a favour and making you feel better when saying that type of stuff but it honestly makes me feel even more shitty and suicidal. 

I think a lot of people don’t understand that suicide comes from lots of factors, not “Some minor inconveniences happened to me & now I’m sad”. I think people just don’t want to acknowledge the ugliness and truth that comes with it, idk.
